overall: The AG found the Fall River City Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any alleged ground: recess talk was interpersonal, side conversations were unproven, and the police chief termination discussion flowed from a noticed topic.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Council deliberated improperly while on recess during the April 8, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the communications that occurred during the recess were not related to Council business but rather pertained to interpersonal dynamics and therefore did not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged Councilors held side conversations during the April 8 meeting and spoke before it about the police chief appointment outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, in the absence of specific evidence of deliberation outside of posted meetings regarding these matters, we do not find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law in these ways.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council discussed the termination of the prior police chief, a topic not listed on the April 8, 2025 meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the discussion about the termination of the former police chief was discussed in the context of the discussion about the Mayor's recommendation to confirm the appointment of Kelly Furtado as Chief of Police, and therefore naturally flowed from discussion of the topic listed on the notice.
